senses.de: A person in the past who was employed by a king or queen to entertain by telling jokes and performing tricks.
senses.ex: The court jester used to wear a multicolored outfit with a cap and bells.

Tips.title: Historical Role
Tips.description: Understand jesters were important in history for humor and truth-telling in royal courts.
Tips.example: The king would often seek the jester's counsel, as jesters could speak frankly.

Tips.title: Iconic Outfit
Tips.description: Remember the jester's outfit with bells is symbolic of their profession and playful nature.
Tips.example: At the medieval fair, many performers dressed as jesters, complete with iconic bells.

Tips.title: Not Just Foolish
Tips.description: Jesters were witty and intelligent, not simply foolish, despite modern misconceptions.
Tips.example: The jester crafted his jokes to cleverly mock the nobility without offending them.

senses.de: A person who often makes attempts to be funny or to make people laugh.
senses.ex: John is always the jester of the group, always ready with a joke or funny comment.

Tips.title: Group Entertainer
Tips.description: Know that a jester in a group brings laughter to friends but should avoid being offensive.
Tips.example: Sara, the group's jester, lightened the mood with her impersonations.

Tips.title: Social Balance
Tips.description: Balance humor with sensitivity, as being a jester means knowing when jokes are appropriate.
Tips.example: As the jester, Tom knew to keep his humor appropriate for the workplace setting.

senses.de: A specific card in a deck of playing cards, often used as a wild card.
senses.ex: In some card games, the jester can substitute for any other card.

Tips.title: Versatile Card
Tips.description: In card games, the jester or joker can often represent any card, making it very powerful.
Tips.example: She won the round with the jester, triumphantly declaring it to be an ace.

Tips.title: Not in All Games
Tips.description: Know that the jester is not used in every card game, so check the rules before playing.
Tips.example: In this game, we don't use the jesters, so please remove them from the deck.

buffoon.wordDefinition:
A buffoon is someone who is considered foolish and often makes people laugh unintentionally due to their silly behavior, while a jester is a professional entertainer who makes people laugh deliberately.

Buffoon is applicable when describing someone's natural behavior or demeanor, while jester is applicable when someone professionally entertains the public through humor and tricks.

Essentially, a buffoon is a fool, while a jester is someone who gets paid to be funny.

clown.wordDefinition:
The main difference between the words clown and jester is that a jester is usually associated with the medieval courts of kings and queens, while a clown is a professional performer who usually wears makeup and performs at circuses or children's parties.

Clowns are performers who wear exaggerated makeup and costumes to create a unique character. They are often associated with circuses and perform a variety of acts, including juggling, magic, and physical comedy.

A jester is a historical figure who provided entertainment for royalty, while a clown is a modern-day performer who entertains audiences at circuses and other events.

comedian.wordDefinition:
A comedian is a person who makes people laugh through jokes, stories, and other forms of humorous entertainment. They are usually professional performers that are hired to provide entertainment.

Comedians can be found in various forms of media such as stand-up, television, and movies.

entertain.wordDefinition:
Entertain means to provide enjoyment or amusement to people, often through singing, dancing, telling jokes, or other performances.

A jester is a specific type of entertainer who is known for their humorous and witty remarks. In medieval times, jesters were often employed by royalty to provide them with entertainment and to poke fun at their guests.

So while both words are related to providing amusement, entertain is a broader term that could refer to many different types of performances, while a jester specifically refers to someone who tells jokes and is known for their humor.

fool.wordDefinition:
A fool is someone who lacks wisdom or common sense and acts foolishly or makes foolish decisions.

While both words are associated with humor and jesting, a fool is generally seen as a negative trait or person, while a jester is seen as a positive and entertaining figure.

Additionally, while a fool's actions or decisions may unintentionally result in humor, a jester's performance is intentionally comedic and skilled.

A fool is someone who lacks wisdom, while a jester is an entertainer who brings joy and humor to their audience.

harlequin.wordDefinition:
Harlequin and jester are both historically associated with entertainment and clowning but they have different meanings.

Harlequin is a character from Italian theater known for his multicolored outfit and acrobatic performances. Harlequin has since been used to describe things that are brightly colored or checkered.

Harlequin is associated with colorful clothing and acrobatic performances, while a jester is known for making jokes and entertaining royalty.

mummer.wordDefinition:
A mummer is a performer who participates in a traditional folk play usually around Christmastime. Mummers wear masks or costumes and go from house to house performing comedic skits.

A jester is a professional entertainer while a mummer is a performer who participates in a specific traditional folk play.

prankster.wordDefinition:
A prankster is someone who enjoys playing tricks on other people. Pranksters often plan and execute elaborate practical jokes, sometimes at other people's expense.

A jester is someone who makes people laugh with jokes and performances, while a prankster is someone who enjoys tricking others with practical jokes.

trickster.wordDefinition:
A trickster is a person or spirit who plays tricks or practical jokes on people, often with a more malicious intention.

Tricksters are found in many cultures as figures of folklore, mythology, and literature.

A jester is an entertainer while a trickster is a prankster.

A jester would be applicable in a more formal setting, entertaining a royal court, while a trickster would be applicable in a more informal setting, pulling pranks on friends or enemies.
